headline: SoftBank chief Masayoshi Son said that even he is worried about AI safety, warning that superintelligence in the wrong hands could become "super dangerous".
score_reason: Fresh on-record warning from a major AI investor; read through the Japan Times copy of Bloomberg's report.
importance_line: It affects governments and investors weighing AI safety against speed, but Son offered a call for cooperation, not a specific safety measure.
summary: Bloomberg reports, in a story the Japan Times carries, that SoftBank Group chief Masayoshi Son, long a strong believer in AI, said at a forum in Kyoto on Sunday that countries must build trust and work together because powerful AI can become "super dangerous" in the wrong hands. Bloomberg notes that SoftBank has put nearly $65 billion into OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, and that Son also repeated his projection that AI will account for at least 20% of global economic output by 2040.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403); text read on the Japan Times, which carries Bloomberg's story by Mayumi Negishi. URL is the Bloomberg original from the pool. The same event had White House adviser Michael Kratsios announce a 17-country AI-for-science push that did not include China.
